_comment: The servers this repo actually has, one entry each. See SERVERS.md.
There is exactly ONE game entry on purpose. This file previously held five
configurations that each started a vite dev server (dev, dev-alt, dev-alt2,
dev-auto, and rive-test, which was a bare `npx vite`). Every dev server
carries the /__tuning writer from vite.config.js, so a second one is not a
duplicate — any tab still pointed at it can POST its boot-time snapshot over
path/src/imported-tuning.json and silently revert hours of tuning. A picker
with five ways to make that mistake is a trap.
`workbench` is the one to start. It is read-only, it is the index of every
tool in the repo, and it links to whatever else is running - including the
game, whose port it resolves live because vite's port moves every restart.
autoPort where the server honours PORT (vite.config.js and csv-editor.mjs
both do) so two sessions never collide. Fixed 5178 for the workbench: a port
that never moves is the entire point of that one.
The two pickers are fixed-port on purpose and for the opposite reason to
the game: they are read-only render servers that write only their own shots
directory, they cannot touch tuning, and each one owns its port so both can
be up at once. They collide with nothing except a second copy of themselves,
which is what the EADDRINUSE message in atlas-render/server.mjs is for.

`workbench` ATTACHES (url, no command) and `workbench-start` is the one that starts a hub. That way round because the harness picks `workbench` by name, and the hub is a singleton on a fixed port that is meant to be left running - so the common case for any session is 'show me the workbench', not 'own it'. Starting a second one on 5178 fails the harness's port pre-check before `npm run hub` (which is idempotent and would just say 'already running') ever gets to run. Use workbench-start only when nothing is up. Never fix this with autoPort: a moving port is the exact problem the workbench exists to solve.

configurations.name: levelup-look
configurations._comment: The built level-up look page (npm run looks:levelup builds dist-levelup-look first). A render server: writes its own shots dir and the seal motion file on Save only; it cannot touch tuning.

configurations.name: ball-lab
configurations._comment: ATTACHES to a ball lab that is already up (url, no command). A localhost url here must be the ORIGIN only, so the page itself is at /tools/looks/ball-lab.html — navigate there after attaching; / is a 404. Use ball-lab-start when nothing is listening.

configurations.name: ball-lab-start
configurations._comment: The built ball lab (npm run looks:ball builds dist-ball-lab first). A render server: writes its own shots dir, the lab's preset, and — only on the page's own 'write to config.js' — splices config.js via tools/apply-ball-lab.mjs. It never touches imported-tuning.json except to CLEAR values the splice replaced.
